transcript: I have to. You have to have to talk about Once Upon One More Time, which I saw early in previews, and this still has not officially opened yet. Opening day is going to be this week on June 22nd, so we will be getting official reviews then. I'm very intrigued about how they turn out. But I have to talk about the show, because if you follow me for a while, you know that I saw this production. Indeed, and I had a lot of fun, but it felt like a show that needed a ton of work. And when it decided to come to Broadway with the exact same creative team, I was a little hesitant about whether that work was being done. And I could not have been more wrong. This show has done so much work from its out of town and even during the preview period that you could see show twice in the same week and it would be completely different. In fact, I have to go see it again because I know the show that I saw in early previews is no longer what it is now. They've added songs, they've rewritten entire scenes. The things that I was hesitant on was the overall design. And when I walked in and saw this, I was like, oh, they really didn't change the design at all. Fortunately, once you get past the pre show vibe, which I think is one of the worst parts, Of the show right now. It really comes to life when the show is on stage. The projections are better, there's more set pieces, costumes. Went from this in DC to now this on Broadway. Snow white's costume alone is the most magnificent transformation. And like I said, the script has been going through a massive amount of changes even since I just saw it a few weeks ago. I do have a major issue with just the premise of the show that I don't think is going to get worked out. But for me that's forgivable because the show itself is still a ton of fun. And while I don't think it's as clever as an an Juliet, I feel like the production quality is definitely on par. And they're just both so much fun to watch. And you are going to hear a lot of people compare the 2 because one they share a lot of the same songs, they have a lot of the same themes. Uh, it would be a wild to show day to do them both back to back. But honestly I think they're both a ton of fun to watch. And the choreo is freaking amazing. As he did in DC, Justin Corrine does definitely steal this show here. Also, Jen Samard is a new addition to the Broadway production and is freaking amazing. I don't know why Adam Godly is doing this following the Lemon Trilogy, but I have seems like he's Having a blast, so I love that journey for him. If you are looking for a deep theater going experience, you can definitely skip this one. But if you want a good fun time out and you really love Britney Spears music and you wanna see some freaking amazing choreo, go see Once Upon One More Time. I love that they have changed so much of the show and I cannot wait to see it again in its final form post opening this week.
